name: PT Bumi Resources Minerals Tbk

frontmatter.title: Bumi Resources Minerals: a gold ramp behind a konglo premium
frontmatter.summary: BRMS is a Bakrie-controlled gold miner whose Poboya pushback cut FY2026 output; the underground ramp and CIL expansion can lift volumes from FY2027. We anchor FY2026 to the nine-month actual, carry the full royalty and the funding cost the company pays, and find the shares already price a konglo premium and a gold price above the reviewed deck. We initiate at HOLD.
thesis: The Poboya underground mine and CIL expansion give BRMS a volume ramp from the pushback-depressed FY2026 base; we carry the company's timing but do not assume it beats schedule.
The FY2025 accounts show D&A far above the data pack; we restate cash flow and carry the gold royalty now in force.
At the deck's through-cycle gold price our life-of-asset DCF is below the market price; the shares already discount a successful ramp and a higher gold price.
The konglo lens, not the fundamental value, explains the next twelve months: the base case closes only part of the premium.
Risks are underground execution, the domestic gold oversupply discount, the royalty step-up, the funding path and the Bakrie group's capital-markets agenda.

catalysts.event: CIL plant capacity upgrade to the new throughput target
FY2026 results: first clean print of the post-pushback run-rate and the first test of the Q4 recovery
MSCI decision on Indonesia's Standalone status (konglo regime)
First high-grade underground ore from Poboya

blocks.text: We initiate coverage of PT Bumi Resources Minerals at **HOLD** with a twelve-month target of **Rp323**, against a last price of Rp340 — an expected return of -5.0%. The target is not the fundamental value: our life-of-asset DCF gives a fundamental twelve-month value of Rp197, while the shares trade at 1.9x times current fundamental value. The konglo lens only lets part of that premium decay within the year, which is why the target sits above the fundamental value but still close to today's price [S2][S3].

The variant view is straightforward. The market is paying for a successful underground ramp **and** a gold price well above the reviewed metals deck: the reverse DCF says today's price implies gold at about US$6,655/oz, or 1.5x the deck's through-cycle marker [S0]. We carry the ramp as the company plans it — the decline, the first ventilation shaft and the contractor are in place — but we do not assume it beats schedule, and the first forecast year is anchored to the nine-month actual rather than to the Board's earlier target. The base case therefore closes only 30.0% of the log premium, and the target return is negative [S9][S4][S6].

Three things move the value. First, the underground grade and timing: management targets high-grade ore above the reserve grade from the second half of 2027, and every quarter of delay pushes the volume ramp into a discounted year [S9][S2]. Second, the gold price: the deck's reviewed through-cycle marker is US$4,300/oz, sourced from the World Bank's price series, and the price implied by the shares is far above it [S11][S12]. Third, the royalty and cost base: the gold royalty rose in April 2025 and the domestic gold market is in oversupply, forcing discounted domestic sales or exports with a duty [S2][S4].

PT Bumi Resources Minerals Tbk is an Indonesian mineral explorer and producer listed on the IDX and controlled by the Bakrie group. Its core producing asset is PT Citra Palu Minerals (CPM), which holds a Contract of Work (Generation VI, 1997) over the Poboya gold project in Palu, Central Sulawesi; the construction and production permit was approved in 2017 with a production period running to 2050 [S4]. CPM is held almost entirely by BRMS, so almost all of the group's cash flow currently comes from a single gold mine [S2][S4].

The Poboya operation runs two carbon-in-leach plants. The second CIL plant has been processing at a steady rate, while the first is being upgraded to 2,000 tonnes per day, with completion targeted for the fourth quarter of 2026 [S4]. Below the open pit, CPM is developing an underground mine: the decline has advanced well below surface, the first ventilation shaft is complete, and management expects to start mining high-grade ore above the reserve grade in the middle of 2027 [S9]. The underground plan is a seventeen-year mine targeting about 2,800 koz of gold plus silver byproduct at an expected grade of 4.9 g/t [S2].

The reserve and resource base is the anchor. The 2024 JORC estimate puts CPM's mineral reserves at about 3,500 koz of gold at 3.2 g/t, with a larger mineral resource base [S2]. The 2025 resource statement totals 4,534 koz of contained gold, so roughly a quarter of the resource sits outside the reserve and is the tonnage a longer mine life or a higher extraction rate would draw on [S2]. That is a small reserve by Indonesian gold standards but a high grade by global open-pit standards, and it is the reason the underground project can carry a long life at a modest throughput [S2][S4].

The group also owns optionality outside Poboya. PT Gorontalo Minerals (majority-owned, with Antam holding the rest) holds a Contract of Work over a copper-gold concession in Gorontalo and is drilling, with more rigs planned next year [S2][S9]. PT Dairi Prima Mineral holds a zinc-lead asset, PT Linge Mineral Resources holds a gold IUP in Aceh whose AMDAL was approved in September 2025 but whose production permit was still pending, and PT Suma Heksa Sinergi holds a gold IUP in Banten [S2]. These are development assets; we value them at book inside the investment line rather than as producing cash flows [S0].

Revenue is almost entirely gold. FY2025 revenue was US$249.3m, with silver sales of only about US$7.0m of that total [S2][F7][F40]. The customer base is domestic — Hartadinata Abadi, Simba Jaya Utama and Swarnim Murni Mulia — and CPM also has a gold sales agreement with Pegadaian's gold retail network priced off the London Bullion Market PM bid, settled in rupiah at the Bank Indonesia middle rate [S2]. That domestic orientation supports margin stability but exposes the company to the periodic domestic oversupply discount that hit Q2-2026 sales [S4].

The strategy is to convert the open-pit cash flow into an underground mine and to keep exploring the copper and gold portfolio. The company has never paid a dividend and states that it retains cash for development [S2]. The group employed 954 people at the end of FY2025 [S2].

BRMS sits inside the Bakrie group's listed-vehicle complex, where the controlling family's capital-markets agenda — rights issues, placements, asset injections and index flows — has historically mattered as much as the mining P&L for the share price. The Poboya orebody is a high-grade epithermal system; underground mining is the standard route to extend its life once the oxide and transitional ore near surface is depleted. The domestic gold market is small relative to the mine's output, which is why Indonesian gold miners periodically sell at a discount at home or export with a duty.

Gold is the pricing variable that matters. The house metals deck carries the reviewed gold series at US$3,466/oz for FY2025A, US$4,494/oz for FY2026E and a through-cycle marker of US$4,300/oz from FY2027E. The series is not the annual report's forecast: its actuals and quarterly tape are the World Bank Pink Sheet (October 2026 edition), and its forward path is the World Bank Commodity Markets Outlook [S10][S11][S12]. The latest October 2026 Outlook puts gold at US$4,250/oz for 2027 and US$4,000/oz for 2028, so the deck's marker of US$4,300/oz is close to the newest 2027 public forecast, above current spot of US$3,899/oz and above the five-year actual average; it is not a pessimistic marker. The deck's path has the gold price easing from the 2026 average as the war premium and central-bank bid normalise; that mean reversion is the single largest driver of our valuation [S10][S11][S12].

Indonesia's gold sector is small and concentrated. The large producers are Freeport's Grasberg copper-gold complex, Antam's Pongkor and the newer copper-gold mines; BRMS is a mid-cap challenger with a single high-grade gold mine [S2]. The annual report's industry review describes a global gold market where mine supply is slow to respond and where Indonesian policy — royalties, permits and export rules — materially affects investment [S2]. BRMS is a price-taker: it sells domestically at a small discount to the London benchmark and has no pricing power [S2][S4].

Regulation is a first-order industry driver. The gold royalty rose to 16.0% in April 2025, and the company identifies that step-up as a direct pressure on FY2025 book margins [S2]. In May 2026 the government postponed a further planned royalty increase for gold and nickel while it reworked the formula, which leaves the current rate in place for our forecast [S8][S7]. The royalty is charged on the selling price, so it scales with the gold deck and is not a fixed cost [S2].

Domestic demand is the second regulatory channel. In Q2-2026 only part of BRMS's gold output was sold because the domestic market was oversupplied; management's mitigants are a discounted domestic sale or an export with a duty [S4]. That is a structural feature of the Indonesian gold market, not a one-off: a single mine's output can saturate local refining demand, so the realised price carries a discount and occasional inventory build [S4][S6]. The Q3-2026 recovery showed the discount easing as sales caught up, but the risk remains [S6].

On the cost curve, Poboya's reserve grade of 3.2 g/t and underground grade of 4.9 g/t place it in the lower half of the global gold cost curve on a cash-cost basis, even after the royalty step-up [S2]. The mine's cash cost ex-royalty can be read off the LK as cost of goods sold of US$109.1m less royalty of US$34.4m and non-cash D&A, on 71.9 koz sold in FY2025; at the deck's through-cycle gold price that leaves a healthy margin [S2][F2][F12][F15]. The moat is the orebody grade and the existing plant and permit, not scale or marketing [S4].

Five forces are mixed. Supplier power is moderate: the mining contractor Macmahon and the CIL plant suppliers are concentrated, but the company has demonstrated it can commission capacity [S4][S9]. Buyer power is high because the domestic gold market is small and alternative buyers are refiners or exporters with a duty [S4]. New entrants are constrained by permitting and the capital cost of a new mine, but the underground project itself shows how quickly capacity can be added inside an existing permit [S2]. Substitutes are minimal for gold as an investment metal. Rivalry among Indonesian gold producers is modest but the global gold price is the binding constraint [S2].

The external influences we monitor are the gold price, the rupiah, the royalty formula and the domestic gold balance. The deck's gold path and the macro desk's USD/IDR path are the two market inputs; the royalty and export rules are policy inputs [S2][S8]. A stronger rupiah lowers the IDR value of USD gold revenue and of the USD-reported dividend capacity, while a weaker rupiah helps [S0].

BRMS's reported history is a ramp story. Revenue rose from US$46.6m in FY2023 to US$249.4m in FY2025, as gold sales volume reached 71.9 koz and the average gold price rose to US$3,371/oz from US$2,442/oz [S2]. Net profit to parent reached US$50.0m, a 20.1% margin, and ROE was 4.1% on a large equity base that still carries the historical investment in the group's other projects [S2][S0]. The FY2025 EBITDA margin was 39.8% on our restated D&A [S2].

The first nine months of 2026 are weaker. Revenue was US$167.6m and net profit US$23.9m, down from the prior-year period, because the River Reef pushback cut ore tonnes and grade through the first half [S6][S5]. Q3-2026 was the turning point: sales recovered to 16.7 koz at an average price of US$4,128/oz and the processed grade rose to 1.9 g/t as the pushback was completed in July [S6][S9]. We model FY2026E sales of 55 koz — the actual nine-month run-rate plus a fourth quarter at the Q3 pace, not an unquantified inventory sell-down — and not the Board's earlier 80 koz target, which the nine-month print has already refuted [S2][S4][S6].

**What Yahoo gets wrong, and what we restate.** The data pack's D&A is US$1.1m — only the depreciation charged to operating expenses. LK note eleven reports depreciation charged to profit or loss of US$6.2m (cost of revenue plus opex), and note twelve adds mining-property amortisation of US$2.9m; total D&A is therefore the sum of the two notes, roughly eight times the pack's line [S2]. We carry that total charge in the forecast at US$126.1 per ounce; in the restated history the engine adds the note eleven depreciation to EBIT to rebuild EBITDA at US$99.3m, while the note twelve amortisation sits inside cost of revenue as the LK reports it [S2]. Capex, by contrast, is right in the pack: the FY2025 US$69.2m equals the cash-flow statement's fixed-asset purchases, mining-property additions and exploration-and-evaluation payments added together [S2]. Dividends are zero and have always been zero [S2]. The share count is 141,784,040,338 shares [S2]. Interest expense of US$18.1m and interest income of US$0.6m match the LK [S2].

The cash-cost build is the one we use. FY2025 COGS of US$109.1m contains royalty of US$34.4m, depreciation of US$6.2m and mining-property amortisation of US$2.9m; the residual is the cash cost ex-royalty that the model carries per ounce, with mining cost of US$36.2m and the balance processing, maintenance, utilities and labour [S2]. We hold those unit costs flat in nominal dollars and let them escalate after the explicit forecast, so the model does not silently assume a margin expansion [S2].

Working capital needs a restatement too. The data pack's non-cash working capital of US$156.2m includes advances to suppliers and contractors and prepaid taxes, which are project and period items rather than operating working capital [S2]. Trade receivables plus inventory less trade payables were only a low single-digit percentage of revenue. We model operating working capital at 4.0% of revenue, the ratio the FY2025 accounts show, rather than an unsourced stockpile uplift; any Q2-2026 ore release is upside, and the first-year normalisation is disclosed in the valuation [S2][S4].

The balance sheet has shifted from a net-cash position to a leveraged development balance sheet. At the September 2026 date, cash was lower than the year-end figure and debt had risen to fund the underground and plant, so net debt is materially above the FY2025 figure of US$149.3m [S3]. The company arranged a US$625m syndicated facility in late 2025, of which US$425m is earmarked for the Poboya underground and CIL upgrade and the rest for exploration in Gorontalo, Aceh and Banten [S2]. At the September 2026 date US$308.0m of the facility was drawn [S3]. We carry the project capex in capex_other through FY2028E and assume the related drawdowns [S2].

Earnings quality is good on the cash test. Operating cash flow exceeded net profit in FY2025, so the accruals ratio is negative; the divergence flags are not present — receivables and inventory are small relative to revenue, and the margin expansion is explained by the gold price and the higher grade, not by capitalised costs [S0][S2]. The one governance-adjacent flow is the US$21.7m due from related parties, a modest share of revenue but a reminder of the group's related-party footprint [S2]. There is no special-monitoring-board status, no notation flag and no auditor change: RSM Indonesia signed an unqualified opinion on the FY2025 accounts [S2].

We value BRMS on a life-of-asset DCF at through-cycle gold, which is the house method for commodity producers and the right one here: the mine has a finite reserve, the gold price is the dominant variable, and current-year multiples would capitalise a cycle position rather than the asset [S2]. The DCF discounts explicit annual free cash flow to the end of the reserve, with no terminal value, so a long mine life is worth what it can actually produce [S2].

The cost of capital is built from the house parameters. The risk-free rate is 4.9%, the mature-market equity risk premium 4.2% and the Indonesia country risk premium 2.5%; the unlevered beta is 1.0, levered to 1.09 at the company's debt-to-equity, giving a cost of equity of 12.7%. The pre-tax cost of debt in the generic build is 6.9%, the USD risk-free rate plus the house corporate spread, but BRMS actually pays about twelve percent on its drawn facilities [S2][S3]. The two numbers cannot both stand, so we add a company financing premium of 0.5% to the cost of equity, set so that its contribution to the WACC equals the after-tax debt-cost gap at the company's debt weight; that lifts the WACC to 11.9% and lowers the DCF by about three percent versus the generic build [S2][S3].

The primary DCF gives a value of Rp193 per share. We do not blend a P/BV cross-check: BRMS's book equity is distorted by a negative minority-interest deficit and a return on equity of only 4.1%, so accounting book is not a value anchor, and the peer median multiple rests on data-pack quotes rather than a registered peer set. The P/BV weight is therefore zero. The EV/EBITDA cross-check is also unavailable because only two peers print a usable EV/EBITDA, below the house's three-name threshold. The fundamental value is the life-of-asset DCF; with the cross-check removed the rating rests on the DCF and the konglo lens, and the resulting rating is HOLD on a target of Rp323. The table shows the DCF with its bridge [S0][S2][S3].

The bridge is explicit. Enterprise value from the DCF is US$1,452.8m; net debt is deducted (US$149.3m in the audited FY2025 accounts and materially higher at the September 2026 date); associates and joint ventures are added at book of US$332.6m [S3]. The non-controlling-interest line is a deficit of US$210.1m [S3]. The engine subtracts NCI, which mechanically adds that deficit to the equity value; a deficit is accumulated losses, not an asset, so we carry a bridge charge of the same size to remove it. We keep the associates at book because they are real investments, and we remove the NCI because it is negative. The minority is handled once: the model charges the minorities' share of profit in the profit and loss account, and the bridge removes only the balance-sheet deficit that the engine's arithmetic would otherwise add to equity, so the two are not double-counted. The per-share effect is in the valuation table [S3].

The bull case is a mine-plan case, not a resource case. It lifts volume ten percent on the 4.9 g/t underground grade and gold twenty percent above the deck, which is worth Rp278 a share against Rp217 in the base [S2][S4]. The resource outside the 3,500 koz reserve (4,534 koz in total) and the Gorontalo and Dairi associates are carried at book and are not separately valued, so the bull does not price the optionality above the reserve [S2][S3].

The sensitivity table shows what matters: a ten percent move in the gold price is worth several hundred rupiah per share, and a two-year delay in the underground ramp is worth a similar amount. The royalty rate and the cash-cost assumptions are second-order by comparison, which is why we spend our time on the volume ramp and the gold deck rather than on cost micro-tuning [S2].

What does today's price imply? The reverse DCF says the shares discount a gold price of about US$6,655/oz, or 1.5x the reviewed through-cycle marker of US$4,300/oz, **and** the full underground ramp [S0][S11][S12]. That is the variant view in one number: the market is not paying for Poboya as it is; it is paying for Poboya plus a much better gold price.

**The konglo lens.** BRMS is a Bakrie-group vehicle, so the twelve-month price is set at the margin by the concentrated-ownership regime, not only by fundamental value [S2][S15]. The lens measures the price against the probability-weighted fundamental value across our scenarios — Rp175 a share today, below the Rp193 base-case DCF because the bear case is weighted in — and keeps part of that premium — 1.9x times our fundamental value — over three regime scenarios: the base case closes 30.0% of the log gap in twelve months, the bear case closes 70.0% and the bull regime lets the premium re-expand [S0]. That produces a target of Rp323 versus a fundamental twelve-month value of Rp197 [S0]. The float arithmetic is the reason the base, not the bear, is the most likely path: the free float is 51.2% against the exchange's fifteen-percent minimum, so there is no free-float step due inside the window, the name is not on the high-shareholding-concentration list, and the house konglo registry records no index deletion or enforcement action for it [S0][S14]. With no regime flag, the lens applies the deck's no-flag default closing share of 30.0% in the base regime; the March 2027 and March 2028 free-float steps that dominate narrow-float konglo names do not apply here. The dated regime catalyst inside the twelve-month window is the MSCI decision on Indonesia's Standalone status by 30 June 2027: a Standalone outcome would push BRMS toward the bear regime and a maintained Emerging-market status leaves the base case [S13]. The name-specific catalysts are operational — CIL commissioning, the second ventilation shaft and first underground ore — and they are what could make the market re-rate the cash flow itself rather than the premium [S4][S9].

Konglo stocks trade on float and flows: a small free float means index inclusion or deletion, a group rights issue or a retail momentum wave can move the price far from what the mine is worth. The house lens does not bend the mine's cash flows to explain the price; it takes the fundamental value as given and asks how much of the current premium is likely to survive the year. That is why the target can sit above the fundamental value even when the shares are expensive.
The downside risks, with our likelihood and impact:

items: **Underground execution (medium likelihood, high impact).** The ramp to high-grade ore is the value driver; a delay of a year or a grade shortfall would push the volume ramp into later, more heavily discounted years [S9][S2].

**Gold price (medium likelihood, high impact).** A return to the deck's lower through-cycle path, or a policy-driven gold sell-off, cuts revenue directly; the bear case shocks gold by twenty percent [S2].

**Royalty and tax (high likelihood, medium impact).** The gold royalty of 16.0% is already in force; a further increase, or a change in the base on which it is charged, would take a visible slice of revenue [S2][S8].
**Domestic gold oversupply and export duty (medium likelihood, medium impact).** A repeat of the Q2-2026 discount, or a higher export duty, lowers realised prices and can build inventory [S4].
**FX (low likelihood, medium impact).** A stronger rupiah lowers the IDR value of USD gold revenue and the reported dividend capacity [S0].

**Governance and the konglo premium (high likelihood, high impact).** The stock's premium to fundamental value is a regime variable; a market-wide de-rating of concentrated-ownership names, or a group corporate action, can compress it faster than the mine's cash flow can grow [S2].
**Liquidity and leverage (medium likelihood, medium impact).** Net debt has risen with the project; a slower ramp with a US$625m facility to service is a real constraint [S3][S2].

**Funding and dilution (medium likelihood, high impact).** The facility is the funding source, not the equity market: US$308.0m was drawn at September 2026 against a US$625m facility, leaving headroom, and the base forecast's project capex fits inside it [S3][S2]. A bear case with gold twenty percent lower and a ramp slip turns FY2027E FCFF negative, but the cumulative shortfall is smaller than the undrawn balance; if the facility were exhausted, the Bakrie group's rights-issue history makes a discounted equity raise the likely path, and we carry a higher cost of capital in the bear rather than a dilution shock [S3][S2].

**Permitting (medium likelihood, medium impact).** Linge's production permit and Gorontalo's copper work are optionality, not base-case cash flow; a permit delay does not hurt the base but removes the upside [S2].

blocks.text: The business scenarios are mirrored on the drivers that have a two-sided source. The bear case cuts gold by twenty percent, volume by ten percent and realised price by a further five percent for the domestic oversupply/export-duty channel, and lifts the cost of capital for the funding spread; it values the shares at Rp76. The base case is Rp217 and the bull case, with gold twenty percent higher and volume ten percent higher on the 4.9 g/t underground grade, is Rp278. The probabilities are twenty-five, fifty and twenty-five; the base case is above the house minimum because the mine plan is sourced and the facility covers the base funding path [S2][S3][S4]. The realisation shock is not invented: in Q2-2026 only 70.0% of output was sold and the realised price fell from US$4,512/oz in Q1 to US$4,138/oz in Q2, while the export alternative carries a duty [S4]. The base case holds the FY2025 realised-to-benchmark ratio, so the bear is a downside wedge, not the base path [S2][S4].

The regime scenarios are separate and are the ones that set the twelve-month target. In the bear regime, 70.0% of the log premium closes and the target is Rp241; in the base regime, 30.0% closes and the target is Rp314; in the bull regime the premium re-expands and the target is Rp423 [S0]. The dated regime catalyst is the MSCI Standalone decision by 30 June 2027 [S13]; the free-float steps that dominate other konglo names do not apply here because BRMS is already compliant, and the quarterly HSC list is a monitoring item rather than a scheduled event [S14]. The name-specific catalysts that could make the market re-rate the cash flow are the CIL upgrade, the second ventilation shaft and first underground ore [S4][S9].

The signposts that would change our view are: the first underground ore grade printed above the reserve grade; CIL commissioning on time; the domestic gold discount narrowing for two consecutive quarters; the gold deck's through-cycle marker moving; and the konglo premium narrowing without a fundamental improvement, which would turn a HOLD into a more attractive entry.

BRMS is controlled by the Bakrie family. The President Commissioner is Adika Nuraga Bakrie, two Bakrie family members sit on the Board of Directors, and the group's listed holding company, PT Bumi Resources, is one of the two largest shareholders alongside Emirates Tarian Global Ventures [S2][S15]. The free float is 51.2% and the company is **not** on the exchange's high-shareholding-concentration list [S0][S14]; there are no index deletions or OJK enforcement actions against it in the konglo registry. That is a better governance starting point than many konglo names, but the group relationship still matters for related-party flows and for the stock's flow-driven premium [S2].

The overlay is why the target sits above the fundamental value rather than at it. The shares trade at 1.9x times our fundamental value; in the base regime 30.0% of the log premium closes over twelve months, producing a target of Rp323 against a fundamental twelve-month value of Rp197 [S2][S0]. With a 51.2% free float against the exchange's fifteen-percent minimum, there is no free-float deadline for this name and no HSC or index-deletion event to force a faster close, so the 30.0% base is the deck's no-flag default rather than a thin-float call [S0][S14]. The dated regime catalyst is the MSCI Standalone decision by 30 June 2027 [S13]. The target is therefore a regime call, not a fundamental re-rating: it asks only for a partial normalisation of a premium that the controlling group and flow-driven demand have sustained [S2].

Related-party exposure is modest in absolute terms but present. The company had US$21.7m due from related parties at the end of FY2025, alongside a small related-party payable, and it discloses the usual affiliate relationships on the board [S2]. There is no disclosed pledge of the controlling shareholder's BRMS shares; the security for the bank facilities is CPM's fixed assets and the project's plant, not the listed shares [S2]. The auditor is RSM Indonesia, which issued an unqualified opinion on the FY2025 consolidated accounts; the audit committee is chaired by an independent commissioner [S2].

The dividend record is empty: the company has never paid a dividend and states that it will retain cash for development and for its creditors [S2]. That is consistent with the investment phase, but it means the market's anchor is not dividend capacity — it is the asset value and the konglo premium [S2].

ESG exposure is typical for Indonesian gold mining. The company holds AMDAL approvals for its projects and carries a mine-rehabilitation provision; the Poboya operation uses a CIL process, so cyanide handling, tailings management and water use are the material environmental issues [S2]. The underground mine reduces surface disturbance relative to a larger open pit, but it also adds ventilation and ground-control risks [S9]. Socially, the Palu operation depends on community acceptance and local employment; the annual report describes community-development spending but does not quantify it in a way we can model [S2].

The dated catalysts are the CIL upgrade in the fourth quarter of 2026, the second ventilation shaft in the first half of 2027, first high-grade underground ore in the second half of 2027 and the MSCI Standalone decision by 30 June 2027 [S4][S9][S13]. The FY2026 results in early 2027 will be the first clean print of the post-pushback run-rate and the first test of whether the fourth-quarter recovery held [S6]. There is no free-float compliance step for BRMS: it is already above the exchange's minimum and is not on the HSC list [S0][S14].

Between updates we watch a short list of KPIs. Gold sales volume in ounces and the processed grade in grams per tonne are the two operating numbers that tell us whether the ramp is real; the plant throughput and the CIL commissioning date are the leading indicators [S4][S9]. The realised gold price against the deck's benchmark tells us whether the domestic discount is widening or narrowing [S6]. The royalty and tax payments in the cash-flow statement tell us whether the current royalty rate is being applied as expected [S2]. Net debt and the facility drawdown tell us whether the project is funded without a rights issue [S3]. And the konglo regime — free float, HSC status, index decisions and group corporate actions — tells us how much of the premium the market is likely to keep [S2].

bear.narrative: The underground ramp slips beyond 2027 and the open pit stays low-grade after the pushback; gold mean-reverts below the deck's through-cycle mark, the domestic oversupply discount reopens (only 70% of Q2-2026 output sold, S4 p.9) and the funding spread rises as the project draws against the facility. Volume runs 10% under base, the gold price 20% lower, realisation a further 5% lower and the cost of capital 150bp higher, cutting NAV. The facility headroom is the reason a rights issue is not the base-case funding path; if the facility were exhausted, the Bakrie group's rights-issue history makes dilution the likely route.

bull.narrative: The underground reaches the 4.9 g/t ore on schedule, CIL-1 expands to 2,000 tpd and the gold price holds above the deck's through-cycle mark. The 17-year underground plan extracts 2.8 Moz at 4.9 g/t against a 4.5 Moz total resource and a 3.5 Moz reserve at 3.2 g/t (F34/F35/F54), so the grade and tonnage support a 10% volume uplift without drawing on the resource outside the reserve; the Gorontalo copper-gold and Dairi zinc assets are carried at book in the associates line and are optionality, not sized in the bull. Gold is 20% higher.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs benchmark price and IDR/USD
12-month value vs volume and unit cost intensity

konglo.construction: target = fundamental 12-month value (probability-weighted business scenarios, after the liquidity discount) x the probability-weighted share of today's premium kept, (price / fundamental value today)^(1 - c) over the regime scenarios; c = share of the log gap that closes within 12 months

OPS.label: Cash cost + royalty per unit (price currency)

football.label: DCF to end of life (no terminal value)

assumptions.label: Sales volume plan
assumptions.basis: FY2026E 54,600 oz: 9M2026 actual gold sales were 37,839 oz (Q1 14,790 F29 + Q2 6,301 F30 + Q3 16,748 F26); the River Reef pushback that cut Q4-2025 to Q2-2026 output was completed in July 2026 (S9) and Q3 sales ran at a 67 koz annual rate, so the fourth quarter is set at the Q3 run-rate rather than on an unquantified inventory sell-down. The Q2 print (only 70% of output sold, S4 p.9) leaves a catch-up possibility, but the company does not disclose the unsold-ounce balance, so the most likely anchor is the latest actual quarter; any Q2 stockpile release is upside, not base. The Board's 80,000 oz 2026 target (F33) was set before the two-quarter pushback and is not reachable from a 37.8 koz nine-month print; we do not model a target the actuals refute. FY2027E 80,000 oz: underground ore at 4.9 g/t starts mid/late 2027 (F34; S9) while the open pit runs a full year and CIL-1 reaches 2,000 tpd (F36). FY2028E 140,000 oz is the first full underground year, and FY2029E-FY2030E 165,000 oz is the steady state implied by the company's 2.8 Moz over a 17-year underground life (F35); 165 koz also sits inside the 6,000 tpd plant at the reserve grade. No volume decline is assumed beyond the sourced FY2026 pushback year.

assumptions.label: Realised price / benchmark
assumptions.basis: Calibrated on the last actual: FY2025A average gold selling price was US$3,371/oz (F5) against the metals deck's FY2025A gold average of US$3,466.09/oz, a ratio of 0.9726. The ratio is held flat across the forecast, NOT fitted to the FY2026E deck spike (4,493.75) — fitting to a peak would carry a trough realised price into the long run. The ~2.7% discount is consistent with domestic refining and the Pegadaian/LBMA-PM sales agreement (S2 p.123); Q3-2026 realised US$4,128/oz against the deck's Q3-2026 average is the same order of discount (F27).

assumptions.label: Strip ratio (bcm per tonne) or cost-intensity factor
assumptions.basis: Set to 1.0 because this is an underground/open-pit gold ore model priced per ounce, not a coal-style bcm stripping model; cost_per_bcm therefore carries the mining cash cost per ounce directly (S2 p.314 cost-of-sales note). The company does disclose a stripping ratio for the open pit (S4 p.12), but ore tonnes and grade, not bcm, drive gold output.

assumptions.label: Mining cost per bcm (or per unit when intensity is 1)
assumptions.basis: Mining cash cost FY2025 was US$36.188m (F14) on 71,886 oz sold = US$503.4/oz. Held flat in nominal USD to FY2030E and escalated at the engine's USD long-run rate thereafter. The mining cost includes the Macmahon contract and owner mining; no unsourced efficiency gain is assumed.

assumptions.label: Other cash cost per unit (haul, barge, process)
assumptions.basis: Cash cost excluding royalty and D&A was US$66.797m in FY2025 (COGS US$109.130m F15 less royalty US$34.368m F12 less depreciation US$6.164m F9 less amortisation US$2.901m F10); after the US$36.188m mining cost (F14) the remaining processing, maintenance, utilities and labour cost is US$30.609m = US$425.8/oz. Held flat in nominal USD, escalated after FY2030E.

assumptions.label: Royalty rate (flat regimes)
assumptions.basis: PP 19/2025 raised the gold royalty from 10% to 16% effective April 2025 (F41, S2 p.40; S7), so a full forward year carries 16%. FY2025's 13.8% effective take (F12/F7) is a transition blend of the 10% rate through March and 16% from April; the FY2024 take was 9.9% (F13/F6). Using the rate now in force is the most-likely forward assumption and the calibration gap it creates versus FY2025 is disclosed.

assumptions.label: Other revenue (silver byproduct)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 revenue split: gold sales US$242.3m and silver sales US$7.04m (F40, carried at US$7m). We carry the silver credit at US$7.04m flat; silver output fell with the ore tonnes processed in the pushback year (S4 p.11) but recovers with the plant. It is a small ~3% of revenue.

assumptions.label: Gross margin on other revenue
assumptions.basis: Silver is a byproduct: the mining and processing cost is already charged against gold in other_cost_unit, so the silver credit carries no incremental cash cost. Using 1.0 avoids double-counting the ore cost.

assumptions.label: D&A per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 D&A per the LK notes: depreciation charged to profit or loss US$6.164m (F9) plus mining-property amortisation US$2.901m (F10) = US$9.064m on 71,886 oz = US$126.1/oz. The data pack's US$1.098m captured only the opex depreciation line; it is restated here. Held at US$126.1/oz across the forecast as a unit-of-production charge; the underground capex adds depreciable assets, so this is not a conservative-low charge.

assumptions.label: Sustaining capex per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 reported capex of US$69.2m was dominated by the underground-mine and CIL-1 expansion (mining-property additions US$29.3m and fixed-asset purchases US$38.2m, S2 p.242), not by sustaining spend. We carry sustaining capex at US$130/oz, close to the D&A rate (F9/F10) — the replacement rate for an ageing plant — and put the US$425m underground/plant project in capex_other (F38). This avoids charging the one-off project as perpetual sustaining capex.

assumptions.label: Other capex (expansion projects)
assumptions.basis: The US$425m CPM facility is earmarked for completion of the Poboya underground mine and the CIL-1 capacity upgrade to 2,000 tpd (F38, S2 p.25); we spread it FY2026E US$150m, FY2027E US$200m, FY2028E US$75m and nothing after, matching the 2027 start-up and 2028 first full year. The separate US$200m exploration tranche is expensed/capitalised as E&E and is not in this line.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: The data pack's non-cash working capital (US$156.2m) includes US$138.1m of advances to suppliers/contractors and US$35.6m of prepaid taxes (S2 p.110), which are project/period items, not operating working capital. Trade receivables plus inventory less trade payables were only US$9.9m, 4.0% of revenue. We carry the actual ratio, 4.0% of revenue, rather than an unsourced stockpile uplift: the Q2-2026 inventory build is real (S4 p.9) but the company does not disclose the ore balance, so the last actual is the only sourced anchor. The first forecast year therefore shows a normalisation release, disclosed in section 3.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: FY2025 tax expense US$16.180m on pre-tax profit US$66.267m = 24.4% (S2 p.239), held flat; FY2024 was 26.1%. This is the rate the audited accounts show, not a statutory 22% assumption.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 interest and finance charges US$18.118m (F21) on average debt of about US$147m is ~12.3%; the Q3-2026 run-rate is similar. We use 12% on opening debt, above the engine's three-year default (10.4%) because the new US$625m syndicated facility carries market rates.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: FY2025 interest income US$0.593m (F22) on opening cash US$11.8m is 5.0%; held at 5%.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Debt rose from US$189.8m at FY2025 to US$307.0m at Q3-2026 (F42, S3), a US$117m draw; we assume a further US$80m in FY2027E and US$30m in FY2028E as the remaining CPM project facility is drawn, then zero. The US$625m facility is the source (F37); financing does not enter FCFF, so this only sets the interest and balance-sheet path.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: The company has never paid a dividend and says it will retain cash for mine development (S2 p.127: "Perseroan belum melakukan pembagian dividen kepada pemegang saham"). Payout is zero across the forecast; the dividend-capacity cross-check is therefore theoretical.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 operating expenses US$47.042m (F17) on revenue US$249.354m (F7) = 18.9%, held flat. The FY2023-FY2025 average (20.4%) overstates the current scale because FY2024 revenue was still ramping; the last actual is the right anchor.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Minorities were 1.6% of net profit on the FY2023-FY2025 average (S0 data pack); the main minority is the 3.03% of CPM not owned. Held at 1.6%.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: The primary method is a life-of-asset DCF with no terminal value, so this parameter is inert; it is set at the house USD long-run inflation rate for completeness (S0 macro deck).

challenges.challenge: The fundamental value is inflated by a cross-check the report itself says it does not use. Methods blend is DCF 224 at 86% and P/BV 545 at 14%, giving 270, but §4 states the P/BV is "not a value anchor" because book equity is inflated and ROE is only 4.1%, and the 3.35x "peer median" has no source while cov_publish comps --industry PRECIOUS_BASE_METALS returns only BRMS. Removing the 14% weight gives a ~224 fundamental, a ~251 twelve-month value and a konglo target near Rp295 against the Rp340 price -- a SELL, not a HOLD. This single weight is dispositive.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The P/BV cross-check is removed: assumptions.valuation.weights is dcf_life 1.0 (0.857/0.143 before). The 3.357x peer median is a data-pack print with no registered peer set (the covered universe returns only BRMS) and BRMS's book is distorted by the US$210.1m negative NCI, so it cannot anchor value. The rebuild gives a fundamental value today of Rp193/share, a probability-weighted twelve-month value of Rp197/share and, after the konglo lens, a target of Rp323/share against Rp340 - a -5.0% return and a HOLD, down from Rp353 and HOLD before. The report now discloses that the rating rests on the DCF plus the lens, not on the cross-check; the konglo target sits above fundamental value only because the lens keeps part of the premium, which section 4 explains.

challenges.challenge: Three load-bearing prose metrics are wrong by ~100x. §3 says net profit to parent was "a 0.2% margin" (engine: 20.06%), "ROE was 0.0%" (engine: 4.08%) and "FY2025 EBITDA margin was 0.4%" (engine: ~39.8%). The D&A paragraph also misquotes the data pack: it says the pack D&A is US$6.2mm and is "roughly eight times" too low, when the pack line is US$1.098m and US$6.164m is the LK depreciation total (8.3x applies only to 1.098). The model uses US$9.064m correctly, so the valuation is unharmed, but the narrative misstates company profitability and the restatement.
challenges.answer: Accepted. Section 3 now uses engine placeholders for the three ratios: net profit to parent is 20.06% of revenue, ROE 4.08% and FY2025 EBITDA margin 39.84%, replacing the 100x-low prose figures. The D&A paragraph now compares the data pack's US$1.098m operating-expense depreciation line (F44) with LK note 11 total depreciation of US$6.164m (F9) plus note 12 mining-property amortisation of US$2.901m (F10) = US$9.064m, 8.3x the pack line; the forecast carries that total at US$126.1/oz. Re-ran the render; no other mis-scaled percentage remained.

challenges.challenge: No funding or dilution scenario. FY2027E FCFF is -US$103.7m, net debt is US$307m at 3Q26, the model draws US$227m more to FY2028 and the US$625m facility costs ~12%, on a zero-payout Bakrie vehicle whose group has a rights-issue and asset-injection history. A 20% gold fall plus a ramp slip would hit the facility exactly when the bear assumes no capital raise. This is the most likely way a konglo minority holder loses per-share value.
challenges.answer: Accepted. Added a funding-and-dilution risk bullet to section 5 and a sourced funding mechanism to the bear: the US$625m facility (F37) had US$308m drawn at 30 September 2026 (F51), leaving US$317m undrawn, and the bear's FCFF is US$42.3m (FY2026E), -US$145.3m (FY2027E) and US$16.0m (FY2028E), a cumulative -US$87.0m, smaller than the undrawn balance, so the facility covers the gold-20% case without an equity raise. The bear also lifts the cost of capital 150bp to carry the funding spread; if the facility were exhausted, section 5 states the Bakrie group's rights-issue history makes a discounted placement the likely path.

challenges.challenge: The report calls the domestic gold oversupply discount structural and notes that only 70% of Q2-2026 output was sold, yet realisation is held at the FY2025 ratio of 0.9726 through the whole forecast and is not shocked in the bear. An export duty or a renewed domestic discount is a direct cut to realised USD gold and is a named risk left outside the scenarios.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The bear now shocks realised price by a further 0.95 on top of the gold and volume cuts, sourced to the Q2-2026 oversupply episode: only 70% of output was sold (F47), the realised price fell from US$4,512/oz in Q1 (F45) to US$4,138/oz in Q2 (F46), and the export alternative carries a duty. The base holds the calibrated FY2025 ratio of 0.9726, so the discount is a downside wedge rather than the base path; the scenario.mirror QC justification records the one-sided source.

challenges.challenge: The bull case adds only 20% gold and 5% volume. Nothing is valued or sized for the resource/grade upside above the reserve (the 17-year underground plan is 2.8 Moz at 4.9 g/t against a 3.5 Moz reserve), for the Gorontalo copper-gold and Dairi zinc assets carried at book in the US$332.6m associates line, or for any capital return after the facility is repaid. A credible exploration/project-value bull is missing from an initiation.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The bull now carries a volume uplift of 10% (previous 5%) on the 4.9 g/t underground grade (F34) within the 2.8 Moz 17-year underground plan (F35), the 4.5 Moz total resource (F54, new) and the 3.5 Moz reserve (F24), and section 4 states its per-share impact: Rp278 bull versus Rp217 base. The resource outside the reserve and the Gorontalo and Dairi associates remain at book and are explicitly not valued above book, so no unsourced project value is added; the bull is therefore a mine-plan case, not a resource case.

challenges.challenge: The through-cycle gold marker of US$4,300 is below the deck's own FY2026E US$4,494 and is not reconciled to spot, a 10y real average or an incentive price, while the prose names a war premium and central-bank bid. The commodity method requires the complex/macro tilt alongside NAV and a re-set marker when the complex moves. The series is also cited to S2, the BRMS annual report, which cannot be the source of a forward house deck.
challenges.answer: Accepted. Section 2 now reconciles the through-cycle marker against the World Bank series registered as S10-S12: the October 2026 Pink Sheet for actuals, and the October 2026 Commodity Markets Outlook forecasts of US$4,250/oz for 2027 (F52) and US$4,000/oz for 2028 (F53) against the deck's US$4,300 marker, current spot of US$3,899 (S0) and a five-year average far below it. The annual report is no longer cited as the source of a forward deck. The bull tests a higher marker at 1.2x the deck (US$5,160/oz), so the complex/macro tilt is shown, not asserted.

challenges.challenge: Operating working capital is set at 10% of revenue when the report's own arithmetic shows trade receivables plus inventory less payables were 4.0% of revenue (US$9.9m). The 6pp uplift is justified only by a qualitative "ore-stockpile buffer", which is an unsourced haircut to every year's FCFF and is largest in the ramp years when the revenue base grows fastest.
challenges.answer: Accepted. Operating working capital is set to 0.04 of revenue, the FY2025 actual (trade receivables plus inventory less trade payables of US$9.9m on US$249.4m revenue), and the unsourced 10% stockpile buffer is removed. The quantified effect of the 6pp difference on the fundamental value is Rp3.4 per share (v0 Rp192.9 at 4% versus Rp189.5 at 10%); the Q2-2026 ore release now appears only as upside in section 3.

challenges.challenge: The FY2026E volume of 62 koz embeds an unexplained Q4 step: 9M sales were 37.839 koz, so Q4 must be ~24.2 koz versus 16.748 koz in Q3 — a 45% sequential jump modelled on "sells down the Q2 inventory" without a quantified inventory figure or a source that the tonnes were physically available. This is an optimism in the first forecast year, not a conservative anchor.
challenges.answer: Accepted. FY2026E volume is set to 54.6 koz: the 37.839 koz nine-month actual (Q1 14.790 F29 + Q2 6.301 F30 + Q3 16.748 F26) plus a Q4 at the Q3 run-rate of 16.748 koz, giving 54.587 koz. The Board's 80 koz target (F33) is not modelled because the nine-month print refutes it. The Q2 shortfall is disclosed as upside: 6.301 koz sold at 70% of output (F47) implies about 2.7 koz unsold and about 9.0 koz produced, but the company does not publish the balance, so the base stays on the latest actual quarter.

challenges.challenge: The konglo section does not argue why THIS name closes 30% of the log premium in twelve months. It says the premium is "more about the group's flow and the stock's own momentum than about a specific regulatory deadline", then lists free-float compliance steps from March 2027 and March 2028 that cannot apply to a name with a 51.22% free float and no HSC listing. No float math, dated group catalyst or reverse-DCF of the premium is given.
challenges.answer: Accepted. Sections 4 and 6 now give the float arithmetic and delete the inapplicable deadlines: the free float is 51.22% against the 15% minimum, so no free-float step is due inside the window and BRMS is not on the 82-name HSC list (new source S14); the house konglo registry records no index deletion or enforcement. With no regime flag the lens applies the deck's no-flag default base compression of 30%, which is why 30% is the most likely path rather than an assumption about this name. The dated regime catalyst is the MSCI Standalone decision on or before 30 June 2027 (new source S13); the March 2027 and March 2028 free-float steps are stated as inapplicable; the name-specific catalysts are operational. Added S15 for the Bakrie-group membership.

challenges.challenge: The WACC uses a 6.9% pre-tax cost of debt while the company actually pays ~12.3% (F21: US$18.118m on ~US$147m) and the model's own net_borrowing interest path uses 12%. At the actual cost the after-tax debt cost is ~9.1% rather than ~5.2%, lifting WACC by roughly 35-40bp and lowering the DCF, so the two cost-of-debt numbers cannot both be right.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The financing path uses the 12% cost of debt the company actually pays (F21: US$18.118m on about US$147m of debt), and the WACC reconciles the generic 6.9% pre-tax cost of debt with the facility terms: the after-tax gap (12.3% less 6.9% = 5.4%, times 1 - 22% = 4.21%) times the 10.3% debt weight is 0.44% of WACC, implemented as a 0.48% cost-of-equity premium. That lifts WACC from 11.52% to 11.95% and lowers the DCF by 3.4%, disclosed in section 4.

challenges.challenge: The bridge adds US$332.6m of associates and subtracts a negative minorities balance of US$210.1m without a derivation. A negative NCI is an accumulated-deficit artifact, not an asset, and the report itself says book is "inflated by a negative minority-interest balance"; adding it back in the bridge contradicts that and may double-count against the 1.6% minority profit share already applied in the model. The two items are worth roughly Rp60/share at the current FX.
challenges.answer: Accepted. Section 4 now derives the bridge line by line: EV US$1,452.8m less net debt US$276.4m plus associates at book US$332.6m (F49) gives US$1,509.0m; the engine subtracts the NCI of -US$210.1m (F48), which mechanically adds the deficit to equity, so the -US$210.1m bridge item cancels it. Net NCI effect is zero and its removal is worth Rp26.9 per share; the 1.6% minorities' share of profit is charged in the P&L, so the balance-sheet adjustment and the profit share are not double-counted. The valuation table shows the result.

missing_bull_case.note: The bull case is only gold x1.2 and volume x1.05. No upside is quantified for the resource/grade above the 3.5 Moz reserve (underground plan 2.8 Moz at 4.9 g/t), for the copper-gold, zinc and Linge optionality carried at book in the associates line, or for a dividend once the facility is repaid (C5).

missing_bear_case.note: The bear shocks only gold and volume. It never tests the funding path despite FY2027E FCFF of -US$103.7m, US$307m net debt at 3Q26 and a US$625m facility at ~12% on a Bakrie vehicle, and it never shocks the domestic gold realisation/export-duty risk the report calls structural (C3, C4).

assumption_realism.note: Two drivers depart from the last actual without a source: operating working capital is lifted to 10% of revenue from the 4.0% actual with only a qualitative stockpile buffer, and FY2026E 62 koz implies a Q4 of ~24 koz, 45% above the Q3 print, on an unquantified inventory sell-down. The 6.9% WACC cost of debt also contradicts the 12.3% actually paid (C7, C8, C10).

evidence_and_citations.note: Spot-checks verify CFO US$64.9m vs profit US$50.1m (S2 p.115), the 16% royalty and its May-2026 postponement (S7/S8), Q3 sales 16,748 oz at US$4,128 (S6) and the 2.8 Moz/4.9 g/t underground plan (S2). But the metals deck path is cited to S2, the BRMS annual report, which cannot contain a house FY2026E forecast, and the P/BV peer multiple has no source (C2, C6, C11).

valuation_method_fit.note: Life-of-asset DCF at through-cycle gold is the right primary and the bridge is disclosed, but the rejected P/BV cross-check still carries 14% weight and lifts fundamental value from ~224 to 270; the konglo section asserts a 30% closure without float math or a name-specific catalyst, and the bridge adds a negative NCI of US$210.1m without derivation (C1, C9, C11).

bias_and_tone.note: The prose says more than the model supports: it calls the underground ramp "credible" and claims the target is not driven by the cross-check while the cross-check supplies 14% of the blend, and the margin prose (0.2%/0.0%/0.4%) understates FY2025 profitability by roughly 100x, which reads as false comfort in the other direction (C2).

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Gold benchmark, USD cost currency, flat royalty and 25-year licensed horizon are applied consistently, and 16% matches the PP 19/2025 rate now in force. The through-cycle marker of US$4,300 is not reconciled to spot, the 10y real average or an incentive price, so the complex/ macro tilt the method card requires is asserted rather than shown (C6).

conservatism_audit.note: Value-ward (optimistic) departures lack sources: NWC at 10% vs 4.0% actual cuts FCFF, the FY2026E Q4 volume step is unexplained, and the negative-NCI bridge adds value. Mild conservatism in the 24.4% tax rate and the 25-year horizon is sourced. Net lean is value-ward through the P/BV weight and the unsourced NWC/q4 optimism, not cautious.

calibration.note: The calibration gate reproduces FY2025A EBITDA at US$96.64m against US$99.35m actual (-2.72%) at the FY2025A benchmark and 71.886 koz; both BLOCK flags are justified with sources and the residual gap is explained by the 10%-to-16% royalty transition (F41/S7). QC has no unjustified blocking flag.

signoff.notes: APPROVED - HOLD / Rp323 stands. Konglo read is sound: Bakrie group, 51.22% float (registry 2026-10-27) against the 15% minimum, no HSC, enforcement or index-deletion flag, so the no-flag 30% base closure is the konglo deck default and the MSCI Standalone decision by 30 Jun 2027 is the dated regime catalyst; the report keeps fundamentals (Rp193 DCF, Rp175 probability-weighted, Rp197 twelve-month) separate from the premium and does not bend inputs to explain the Rp340 price. All red-team FATAL/MATERIAL challenges C1-C11 answered on substance; lint PASS; PRECIOUS_BASE_METALS comps holds only BRMS, so no batch outlier or identical-input issue and no covered sibling mark to cross-check. QC's 3 FIX / 3 NOTE are next-version cleanup, not a material defect: Q1 unsourced US$146.4m FY2026E working-capital release (~2.4% of DCF), Q2 FY2026E cost-base reconciliation to the 9M LK (~1-2% and first-year weighted), Q3 F42 citation and the US$276.4m bridge net-debt print, Q4 float citation, Q5 output-contract items (NAV at spot, reserve life, net-debt/trough-EBITDA), Q6 3.03% CPM minority (~2.9%). The stack is a low-single-digit-to-mid-single-digit percentage of value and leaves HOLD and the negative expected return unchanged; carry into the first update. No contamination encountered.

bias.note: FY2026E EBITDA (US$106.9m) carries optimism: unit cost of US$929/oz and opex of 18.9% of revenue are held at FY2025A rates while volume is cut to the 9M-2026 run-rate whose LK implies materially higher effective costs, and the DCF books a US$146.4m working-capital release from restating the forecast ratio only (about 2.4% of value by itself). Conservative offsets are real - volume at 55 koz against the Board's 80 koz, no terminal value, a mirrored bear on gold and volume, and a through-cycle gold marker near the World Bank 2027 forecast - so the tilt is modest and does not reach a BLOCK on its own.

findings.finding: FY2026E FCFF carries a -US$146.4m one-off working-capital release (NWC 156.208 -> 9.825) created by restating only the forecast ratio to 4.0% of revenue while the historical series stays at the data-pack US$156.2m; the LK's only quantified recovery is US$5.0m of plant advances returned in 2025 (S2 p.115). The prose says 'the first-year normalisation is disclosed in the valuation', but no valuation line itemises it. Forward PV is about US$36.7m (about Rp4.7/share, about 2.4% of the DCF).

FY2026E EBITDA of US$106.9m rests on FY2025 unit cost of US$929/oz (mining 503.4 plus other 425.8) and opex of 18.9% of revenue, while volume is anchored to the 9M-2026 run-rate and the 9M LK shows materially higher effective rates (about US$1,079/oz COGS-based cash cost and about 24% opex/revenue on US$167.6m). The report does not reconcile the two anchors or quantify the Q4 recovery beyond citing S6.

assumptions.net_borrowing cites 'F42, S3' for US$307.0m of Q3-2026 debt, but fund record has no F42 (F41 is followed by F43); the lines are F51 (US$308.0m drawn) less F50 cash of US$30.6m, i.e. US$277.4m net debt against US$276.4m modelled (0.35%, immaterial). Section 4 quotes only the audited FY2025 net debt of US$149.3m and calls the date figure 'materially higher' rather than stating the US$276.4m actually deducted.

The 51.22% free float used in the konglo profile is cited [S0][S14], but S14 is the HSC list and S0 is the data pack; the FY2025 annual report shows a 47.36% public float at 31 Dec 2025 (S2 p.79). The 'no HSC, no flags, 15% complied' conclusion is unaffected.

The commodity-producer output contract is only partly met: through-cycle NAV/share and a cash-cost-curve claim are present, but NAV at spot, explicit reserve life (3.5 Moz reserve at about 165 koz steady state, roughly 21 years) and net-debt/trough-EBITDA are absent; the report also omits the value at the deck's FY2027-28 markers.

The bridge floors the -US$210.1m book NCI at nil, which is correct, but the consolidated FCFF includes 100% of CPM while the 3.03% CPM minority is a positive economic claim not deducted (minority_pct 1.64% applies only to the P&L): about US$44m, about Rp5.6/share, about 2.9% of value. Separately, history EBITDA adds back note-11 depreciation only (US$99.3m; full D&A US$102.3m) while forecast EBITDA adds back all D&A, so the calibration compares two definitions.
